context.body: Before Miriam appears, verse 19 briefly restates horses, chariots, returned water, and Israel’s dry-ground passage.
context.label: Narrative recap

observations.body: Moses and Israel sing first; Miriam later leads the women with tambourines and dances.
observations.label: Who sings

observations.body: The opening line names horse and rider, and Miriam answers with the same image at the close.
observations.label: Horse and rider

observations.body: Sea, deeps, floods, wind, and mighty waters recast the crossing in repeated poetic images.
observations.label: Water language

observations.body: The song gives the enemy a first-person plan to pursue, overtake, divide plunder, and destroy.
observations.label: The enemy speaks

observations.body: The song moves from the sea to peoples who hear, a promised crossing, a mountain, a sanctuary, and enduring reign.
observations.label: Beyond the sea

payload.posture: Notice which actions the song repeats, how its voice moves, and how Miriam’s shorter refrain closes the core Event.
payload.tension: The singers remain beside the sea, while the song reaches forward to peoples, passage, planting, sanctuary, and reign.
payload.title: The Event becomes song
